designStatus: Original source-fit authoring protocols, not actual learner observations or a claim of general cognitive mastery.

protocols.task: Investigate a practical sorting/transfer problem: observe a mixed object collection, choose and explain categories/relationships, propose a testable idea about a material or shape, test it, then construct/use a simple tool and review a short recording in a suitable app. Add a separate everyday-choice transfer case.
evidenceDesign: Retain evidence for categorisation, tentative explanation, relevant observations and purposeful tools rather than sum linked child records.
Ask how an unexpected result affects the idea and what should be checked next.
Use a different natural/daily-life case for transfer; this is bounded framework authoring, not a claim about general intelligence or every worldly relationship.
nearMisses: A finished craft alone credited as all observation/logical-thinking requirements.
Declaring a broad goal attained from topic-link counts.
protocols.transfer: Transfer to an unfamiliar object collection and a new practical problem.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: All component protocols apply, including complete existing whole-claim cases and declared resources. Goal disposition is separately justified by an integrated design and cross-context transfer, not calculated from child dispositions.

protocols.task: Observe familiar objects and suitable pictures/models, then group them using stated observable properties. Explain category membership, overlaps/subgroups and a relationship between the groups; use a hand lens for one fine-detail comparison.
evidenceDesign: Use actual observed attributes rather than an unrelated name rule.
Retain category counts and most/fewest comparison for the whole single-category claim.
For the complete two-attribute claim, use a Venn overlap or Carroll/two-way table, including both/neither cases and relevant cell questions.
nearMisses: Only reciting category labels without assigning objects or explaining a relation.
Confusing an object’s material/function with its colour or picture size.
protocols.transfer: Classify a different collection under a changed pair of properties and explain one reassignment.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete sorting/counting/diagram claims and their inherited primary data/number prerequisites remain intact. Additional category vocabulary and display cases are checked separately when assessing whole-topic mastery; one source task is not a certificate of every prerequisite.

protocols.task: Before a controlled simple investigation, ask for a tentative explanation and predicted result. Use a safe comparison such as an equal object moved by differing pushes under stable conditions, or teacher-prepared ice/water comparisons, record observations and reconsider the proposed explanation.
evidenceDesign: Keep the original child-proposed idea and prediction before showing the result.
State what changed and what was held stable; compare prediction with actual observations.
Use evidence to explain the outcome, identify an observation that would challenge the explanation and propose a further test.
nearMisses: An adult supplies the explanation after the result and the child merely repeats it.
A changed count or temporal sequence treated as proof of one cause.
protocols.transfer: Use another causal setting with a different controlled feature.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Wa retains simple testing/observation/answer; MRQ retains guided comparison; 7Vr includes reporting, evidence-supported conclusion, a new-case prediction and method improvement. The full tlf claim also receives a supplied frog-count/possible-explanation case and a shadow-length/Sun-height case: count change alone does not give cause, relevant observations must fit and a non-fitting result must be recognised. These are task designs, not fabricated learner observations.

protocols.task: Choose suitable safe equipment for a real work/learning purpose: make a small card/fabric object using cutting/shaping/joining, use a lens to examine detail and operate a familiar app for a learning need. Explain what each tool helped accomplish.
evidenceDesign: Choose between plausible alternatives rather than name a tool in isolation.
Use each tool to achieve an actual result and explain a relevant function/feature.
Record assistance, safe handling, storage/cleanup and accessibility of the supplied equipment.
nearMisses: Pointing at tools with no effective use.
Requiring a powered-saw/drill feature inventory merely because the source says appropriate.
protocols.transfer: Choose another tool for a changed material or information need.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: FtCL keeps measured/marked cutting of card/fabric, folding/rolling/shaping, suitable joining and a moving/standing-part case. vJO keeps careful equipment-based observation, description/comparison/identification; SZ includes hardware/software distinction and purposeful app use, with its complete everyday-computer prerequisite checked separately.

protocols.task: Use a controlled observable action/change comparison with familiar materials. The child states what happened to the second object/material and contrasts it with a suitable unchanged comparison.
evidenceDesign: Repeat or vary the action so an observed effect is not merely a coincidence of two unrelated events.
Keep observation and explanation distinguishable in ordinary words.
Where a source illustration is used, state its actual conditions rather than a universal material law.
nearMisses: Only predicting what the adult expects without observing.
Declaring every added material dissolves or every object changes in the same way.
protocols.transfer: Try another safe action/material case and a no-change countercase.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Simple tests and prediction/result comparison have complete primary task cases. No extra material-specific topic is created for each illustrative object.

protocols.task: Compare gentler/stronger pushes of the same ball on the same surface from a marked start, with consistent direction and repeated attempts. Use the evidence to explain an observed difference and predict a new comparable trial.
evidenceDesign: Keep ball, surface, starting conditions and relevant direction stable.
Describe uncertainty or a surprising trial and suggest a method improvement.
Explain the action/result connection without requiring energy equations or a universal more-force/any-distance rule.
nearMisses: Comparing different balls or surfaces and attributing every difference to push strength.
protocols.transfer: Use another controlled movement action or change one declared condition.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole simple-test and reporting/conclusion claims include observation records, oral/written explanation, a new-case prediction and improvement. Suitable simple table, display, diagram/key cases account for the inherited evidence-recording chain.

protocols.task: Use a fictional attendance story with enough information to support a possible reason, plus a second unknown-cause absence; separately compare supplied plant-condition observations for water, light and suitable temperature. Ask for justified connections and what cannot yet be concluded.
evidenceDesign: Avoid collecting actual classmates’ health information or diagnosing from absence.
Distinguish a supplied supported reason from a possible cause with missing evidence.
A plant without rain may still be watered; wilting can have several explanations, so seek relevant information rather than assert one inevitable cause.
nearMisses: Any two events together treated as causal.
Repeating a because-sentence without explaining its link or responding to a changed fact.
protocols.transfer: Offer another everyday rule/reason case, and a plant case where the first proposed cause is contradicted.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete Understanding Why operation includes a child-generated why/how question, explaining a reason and connecting a new idea to known experience. Its teach-back/plan/persistence hard chain receives separate primary cases: explain in own words with an own example, recognise a genuine question/gap when one emerges, plan a simple approach and use a productive response to difficulty. No gap, frustration or positive feeling is fabricated to certify performance. Plant-needs evidence covers water, light and suitable temperature with actual/supplied contrasting observations, not deliberate harmful learner experiments.

protocols.task: Use a previously supported action/material relation to predict a new comparable case. Ask the child to state the conditions and reason before observing the outcome.
evidenceDesign: Prediction follows a relevant proposed explanation or prior evidence, not arbitrary colour matching.
Retain a new situation and an observation that could challenge the prediction.
For weather illustrations, do not teach a categorical no-rain rule from cloud colour; use a defensible controlled nature case instead.
nearMisses: A lucky guess with no reason.
One cloud appearance declared proof of future weather.
protocols.transfer: Change a material/action condition and ask whether the earlier prediction still applies.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete conclusion/report claim retains evidence, reporting, prediction and improvement. The source example does not require advanced meteorology or a country-specific prediction topic.

protocols.task: Invite a tentative grouping/rule from several objects, then choose a deliberate countercase and test a further prediction. Suitable sets include rolling orientations or floating objects with contrasting materials/shapes.
evidenceDesign: The child proposes the idea rather than only follows an adult’s finished rule.
An exception can narrow or replace the explanation; being initially wrong is not failure when the reasoning responds appropriately to evidence.
State conditions and do not infer that roundness alone controls flotation or that every object falls in the same observed order regardless of conditions.
nearMisses: A rule repeated despite a counterexample.
A plate/pin or paper/stone illustration promoted into an unconditional physical law.
protocols.transfer: Use a new object with a feature that distinguishes two possible explanations.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole simple-test, conclusion/prediction and data-explanation cases are retained. No density, fluid-mechanics or formal hypothesis-testing prerequisite is invented for the simple source operation.

protocols.task: Compare a hot and a cool local-weather case plus a rainy case for full clothing evidence. Discuss year-round food/water needs and seasonally available produce using explicitly attributed resource cards; explain a suitable choice and how another locality or new availability information could change it.
evidenceDesign: Use actual weather conditions, not a universal national season calendar or obligatory winter costume.
Basic body needs remain in every season; no winter rule removes water or balanced food, and no adult intake amount is prescribed to a child.

The dated NHB 2010 availability chart is a historical teaching case, not a claim about today’s local market. Its mango/pea contrast and year-round banana countercase demonstrate that not all foods follow the same availability pattern. The 2026 ICAR Delhi summer-field report is a separate dated crop example, not proof of every region’s harvest.
Explain that suitable plant conditions can influence harvest/availability, while transport, storage and preferences also affect choices. A month table alone does not establish a single cause.
nearMisses: A universal summer/winter menu or a claim that a particular food is medically required by season.
Forcing an adult fluid quantity or judging a family’s unfamiliar food as wrong.
Claiming all India has identical weather or current food availability from a 2010 chart.
protocols.transfer: Provide a contrasting locality or changed availability case and ask for an adjusted choice and reason.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Dj retains clothing/equipment and activity choices for at least three weather conditions. Basic Body Needs retains food/energy, water/hydration, sleep/rest-growth and exercise/strength cases. Plant Needs retains water, light and suitable-temperature evidence and predictions. Local material cards instantiate the source’s practical food/clothing context; no seasonal-food or country-climate clone is added.

protocols.task: Use child-suitable materials and tools to cut along marked/measured lines, shape/fold/roll and choose a joining method for a simple useful object. Include card and fabric examples and an actual moving or standing part.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual tool control and an effective work result, with assistance recorded.
Choose a method suited to the material and check the joint rather than merely name glue/tape.
Use suitable safe handling, nearby adult support where appropriate, and tidy/store equipment.
nearMisses: An adult completes all cuts/joins while the work is credited as independent.
protocols.transfer: Change material or purpose and select another suitable method.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete existing FtCL claim is retained; one specific implement does not become a new mastery node.

protocols.task: Use a suitable familiar offline/localised app or player for a learning purpose. Start, pause, resume and adjust/replay a relevant segment in response to a real information need; identify the hardware part and software/app involved.
evidenceDesign: Record whether controls are chosen by the child or indicated step by step by an adult.
For familiar fluent use, change the request so the child cannot repeat only one memorised tap sequence.
Identify two hardware parts, name the app as software, explain what it helped do and retain the everyday-computer prerequisite’s wider examples.
nearMisses: Only pressing a highlighted button without relating it to the learning purpose.
One successful tap credited as complete hardware/software mastery.
protocols.transfer: Use a changed learning clip or another simple familiar app and explain the controls’ effect.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The existing hardware/software plus purposeful-use operation directly contains this source case. Full-topic/prerequisite evidence remains separate from the source component; no advanced media-control or confidence level topic is created.

protocols.task: Observe real objects and pictures/models of a familiar place or activity. Describe/point out specific contrasting attributes and spatial details, then use a hand lens for an appropriate real-object comparison.
evidenceDesign: Retain finer distinguishing details rather than only broad labels.
The observer’s description must match actual visual evidence, not an unrelated memorised story.
Use an appropriate task language/access method; no fixed English phoneme or script inventory is imposed.
nearMisses: Only naming the main pictured object with no detail.
Copying every adult-supplied adjective while unable to identify its referent.
protocols.transfer: Describe a changed representation where a familiar detail is different.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole observation and clear-description claims retain equipment-based detail, comparison/identification, logically ordered information and intelligible communication. Source evidence is not automatic mastery in every language.

protocols.task: Give a real need such as moving small counters into a narrow container without scattering them. The child constructs a simple working funnel/scoop/guide from suitable materials, tests it, uses it and explains how its shape helps.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual construction and functional use, not only a drawing or a decorative model.
The child makes meaningful shaping/joining decisions; adult preparation/support is recorded.
Use a new task condition to check whether the shape still serves the purpose.
nearMisses: A copied label on a non-working model credited as solving the practical need.
protocols.transfer: Build/adapt a tool for a different container/material-transfer problem.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: FtCL retains its complete material/tool-control cases; hi8 uses its permitted physical-model route and requires shape/function/problem explanation. No technical-blueprint, powered-tool or new country/grade tool-building claim is needed.

protocols.task: After actual learning-media use, invite a low-stakes response about what felt familiar, difficult or worth trying next. Offer appropriate access/support and a changed familiar task.
evidenceDesign: Keep operational fluency evidence separate from reported comfort or hesitation.
Competence can coexist with frustration or uncertainty; no forced positive feeling.
Record context/support rather than introduce a stable confidence score or new learner field.
nearMisses: Assuming correct use proves comfort, or hesitation proves lack of operational knowledge.
protocols.transfer: Change the resource or support and retain the changed context.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: This mixed source record keeps actual media-control skill plus contextual response. No confidence-only mastery topic or difficulty clone is created.

supplementaryResources.use: Qualitative support for suitable varied locally available seasonal produce and water needs in heat; adult quantitative prescriptions are not transferred into child tasks.

supplementaryResources.use: Explicitly dated historical month/availability teaching case, visually read back; not a universal current local-market rule.

supplementaryResources.use: Dated Delhi summer crop example and variability across agro-climatic contexts; not an exhaustive food list.

supplementaryResources.title: IMD Delhi Palam climate normals
supplementaryResources.use: Qualified warm/cool local-weather context, with actual locality and period retained rather than a universal Indian season pattern.

selectedPrimaryViewBoundary: The suggestive protocols account for the selected Grades 1–2 view (ages 6–8). Six printed positions also span Balvatika 3; that original source band is retained in the companion record report, rather than inferred to be a Grade 1–2-only source or an age-specific deadline.
